Real Postgres row-level security (app/db.py's enable_row_level_security, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + a tenant_isolation policy keyed on the session's app.tenant_id) enforced against a genuine non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS login role (app_role, tests/conftest.py) -- tests run as this role, since the postgres superuser bypasses RLS regardless of FORCE (CP-011). An explicit role-permission allow-list (app/services/permissions.py, CP-013) covering the three named examples from docs/02 (billing_operator cannot release_strategy, researcher cannot grant_rights, customer cannot view_broker_credentials) plus fail-closed-by-default for any unlisted action. 35 tests total, all passing. 03_economic_journal.notes: Two parts. (1) signal-copier/app/economics.py: fixed the completed_trade_win_rate naming issue flagged in Phase 00 -- renamed the existing (genuinely fill-based) metric to closing_fill_win_rate, kept completed_trade_win_rate as a deprecated alias (same value, so nothing calling it breaks), and added a real completed_lifecycle_win_rate that counts independently completed position episodes (flat -> non-flat -> flat), with break-even episodes tracked separately from wins/losses. A position closed across several partial-exit fills is one episode, not one-per-fill -- the two metrics can disagree (tested) exactly when a losing partial exit is offset by a winning one in the same episode. 928 signal-copier tests pass (12 new). (2) signal-portfolio-commercial/app/models/ledger.py + app/services/ledger.py: the four-book (source/model/platform/follower) append-only economic journal itself -- Numeric/Decimal money fields (never Float), a real Postgres BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger (app/db.py's enforce_append_only) that rejects direct mutation even for the table owner, and append_correction() that fixes a mistake by inserting a new row referencing the original via correction_of, never editing it. This is deliberately NOT a wrapper around app/provider_value.py -- it's a new, generic, multi-book ledger; provider_value.py remains what it was, a narrower single-owner analysis tool. 6 new tests (41 total in this package). ruff/mypy clean both places.

No caller appends real entries yet (Phases 04-07 will). The other docs/04 metrics (Sharpe/Sortino, drawdown, profit factor, tail risk, subscriber-fee ledger) are not built -- tracked as still open, not silently assumed done.

05_publication_customer_copy_lifecycle.notes: Bounded to the durable-publication-intent core of docs/05, mirroring spec/contracts/PublicationIntent.schema.json field-for-field. app/models/publication.py: PublicationIntent with two load-bearing DB-level uniqueness constraints -- idempotency_key globally unique, and (channel, external_strategy_id, portfolio_version_id, action, revision) unique per docs/02's named natural key (a second intent claiming the same tuple with different content is rejected by the database itself, not just application code). app/services/publication.py: enqueue_intent (same key/same body joins one operation and returns the existing row; same key/different body raises IdempotencyConflictError rather than silently picking one) and transition (a fail-closed state-machine over DRAFT/ELIGIBLE/QUEUED/SENDING/ACKNOWLEDGED/UNKNOWN/REJECTED/RECONCILING/SUPERSEDED/TERMINAL -- UNKNOWN can only proceed to RECONCILING, never straight to ACKNOWLEDGED or REJECTED, since that would be exactly the 'blindly retried' shortcut the spec forbids; TERMINAL/SUPERSEDED are absorbing). 8 new tests (70 total). 06_collective2_publisher.notes: app/services/collective2_publisher.py builds (never sends) the API4 Order envelope from a PublicationIntent. The TIF resolution this build was asked to do first was ATTEMPTED and BLOCKED, not guessed: this session tried WebFetch on https://collective2.com/apidoc/v4 to resolve the spec's own flagged conflict (docs documenting TIF0=day/1=GTC but one conditional example using 2) and the request was refused by this environment's egress policy (collective2.com is not an allowed domain), confirmed via /root/.ccr/README.md as an organization policy denial, not a transient failure -- per that file's own instruction, such denials are reported, never retried or routed around. Consequently `Tif` defines ONLY the two undisputed values (DAY=0, GTC=1); the disputed value 2 is not a member and build_order raises UnsupportedTifError defensively if a TIF outside those two is ever produced. Every issued intent currently resolves to DAY (the more conservative of the two undisputed values) via a single `_resolve_tif` function, pending a real per-portfolio TIF policy. Also implements: OPEN/ADD map to a BUY market order, REDUCE to a SELL market order (quantity_basis must be UNITS, an integer whole number, or the build refuses rather than truncating/rounding); STOP_UPDATE/TARGET_UPSERT map to a PriceOnlyModification envelope per docs/06's 'price-only modifications, not general direction/duration/quantity replacement'; CLOSE/ENTRY_CANCEL/STATUS_CORRECTION/STRATEGY_PAUSE/TARGET_REMOVE/TARGET_CLEAR have no mapping yet and raise rather than guessing. 13 new tests (83 total). Load-bearing verification: broke the REDUCE-is-SELL mapping and the fractional-quantity rejection in turn, confirmed the matching tests failed, restored exactly. ruff/mypy clean.
06_collective2_publisher.not_yet_wired: No transport -- nothing calls the real API4 HTTP endpoint (no credentials exist in this environment; CARD-3 platform agreements and a real scoped API4 Bearer key are prerequisites, not yet obtained). No StrategyId/instrument-approval resolution, no C2Symbol/ExchangeSymbol lookup (c2_symbol is passed in by the caller, not resolved here), no OCA/stop-target group reconciliation, no external-acknowledgment readback wired to publication.transition(). Remains BLOCKED for the TIF=2 question specifically -- do not widen the Tif enum without real, captured vendor confirmation, and do not attempt collective2.com again from this environment without the egress policy changing.

Load-bearing verification: broke the demo-only enforcement and the by-symbol exclusion in turn, confirmed the matching tests failed, restored exactly. ruff/mypy clean.
